title: An IMF reserve asset is valued against five currencies
body: The International Monetary Fund created Special Drawing Rights in 1969 to supplement countries' reserves. The IMF's basket includes the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and British pound.
takeaway: Countries can exchange these reserve assets for usable currency even though people cannot spend them in shops.
source: International Monetary Fund, Special Drawing Rights Factsheet (2023)
visual: a balance holding a small stack of plain coins beside an open ledger

title: A 1992 wage rise did not cut jobs in one fast-food study
body: In April 1992 New Jersey raised its minimum wage from 4.25 to 5.05 US dollars an hour. David Card and Alan Krueger surveyed 410 fast-food restaurants in New Jersey and Pennsylvania and found no relative fall in New Jersey employment.
takeaway: A neighbouring region with an unchanged wage can help reveal what might have happened without the rise.
source: Card and Krueger, American Economic Review (1994)
visual: the counter of a modest early nineties fast-food restaurant
